Owner-only records with an elevated reader, and a private file per record: each signed-in user files expense claims and sees only their own, a user whose role is `manager` sees and edits every claim, and a claim's receipt is a private upload that only someone who may read that claim can open. No flow is needed.

content:
# Owner-only records: each user sees and changes only their own expense
# claims, a manager sees and changes every claim, and a claim's receipt is a
# private file that only someone who may read the claim can open.
site_name: "Expense claims"
auth:
  identifier: email
access:
  claims:
    read: owner_or_role:manager     # own rows; every row for a manager
    write: everyone                 # any signed-in user files a claim
    update: owner_or_role:manager
    delete: owner_or_role:manager

model Claim {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  title       String
  amountCents Int      @map("amount_cents")
  receiptUrl  String   @default("") @map("receipt_url")   // what POST /api/_upload returned
  userId      Int      @map("user_id")                    // the owner, set by the framework
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  @@map("claims")
}

check: POST /api/_upload (multipart: `file`, `kind=private`) answers {path, url, filename, size}; store `path` in receipt_url when creating the claim. GET on that path answers 403. GET /api/_signed_url?path=<path>&record_table=claims&record_id=<id> answers {path, url, expires_in} for the owner and for a manager, and the signed path returns the bytes; any other user gets 404 on the claim and 403 on the signature, also after copying the reference into a claim of their own (`this record does not own the file`). In page code: `bm.signedUrl(claim.receipt_url, { record: { table: 'claims', id: claim.id } })`.
notes: `manager` here is the account's own role (`_benmore_users.role`): set it when creating the user (`benmore users <app> create <email> --password-stdin --role manager`) or in the admin panel. A role held only inside a tenant does not widen `owner_or_role:` on a table without the tenant key (`access.how`).
`role:manager` instead of `owner_or_role:manager` would leave a manager with only their own rows (`access.role_mode_rows`).
The owner can edit every column of their own claim. To keep one column out of their hands (an approval state), move it with a workflow: `tasks.status_workflow`.
Store and sign the reference exactly as the upload returned it; on the hosted media CDN it is a full URL (`uploads.gotchas`).
On the hosted platform an upload that would take the account past its media storage allowance answers 507 with code `media_storage_limit` and stores nothing (`uploads.storage_allowance`).
